rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disjointed letters were discussed earlier at the beginning of al-Baqarah.
rows.anchor: أما الكلام على الحروف المقطعة فقد تقدم في أول سورة "البقرة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear Book is the Qur'an, which makes obscure matters plain, explains them, and clarifies them.
rows.anchor: الواضح الجلي، الذي يفصح عن الأشياء المبهمة ويفسرها ويبينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic is the most eloquent, clear, expansive, and expressive language; therefore revelation came in the noblest language, to the noblest messenger, through the noblest angel, in the noblest place and month.
rows.anchor: فلهذا أنزل أشرف الكتب بأشرف اللغات، على أشرف الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “because We revealed to you” explains that the best stories are told through revelation of this Qur'an.
rows.anchor: بسبب إيحائنا إليك هذا القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: People asked the Prophet to tell stories, and the verse about the best stories was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قالوا: يا رسول الله، لو قصصت علينا؟ فنزلت

rows.speaker: سعد
rows.claim: After the Qur'an had been recited to them for a time, people asked for stories; these opening verses were revealed, and later a request for reports led to 39:23.
rows.anchor: عن سعد قال: أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم القرآن، قال: فتلا عليهم زمانا

rows.speaker: عون بن عبد الله
rows.claim: When Companions tired of ordinary reports, they asked for stories between reports and Qur'an; God directed them to the best discourse and best stories.
rows.anchor: عن عون بن عبد الله قال: مل أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is praised as sufficient in place of all other books.
rows.anchor: المشتملة على مدح القرآن، وأنه كاف عن كل ما سواه من الكتب

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: When Umar brought a book from the People of Scripture, the Prophet warned against seeking their reports, which could be false or misbelieved, and said Moses would have followed him if alive.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله؛ أن عمر بن الخطاب أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بكتاب

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن ثابت
rows.claim: Umar offered Torah excerpts copied from a Jewish man in Qurayza; the Prophet objected and said that even Moses, if present, would have to follow him.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن ثابت قال: جاء عمر إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال

rows.speaker: خالد بن عرفطة
rows.claim: Umar disciplined a man for copying Daniel, ordered the writing erased and forbidden, and recounted how the Prophet had censured Umar for copying scripture, stressing the concise, pure revelation given to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: عن خالد بن عرفطة قال: كنت جالسا عند عمر، إذ أتي برجل من عبد القيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report through Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq is strange by this route; he and his teacher were weakened, and al-Bukhari said the report is unsound.
rows.anchor: قال البخاري: لا يصح حديثه

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: As a supporting report, Umar recounts copying Jewish material during the Prophet's life; the Prophet erased it and warned against following confused People of Scripture, and the two men from Hims buried their copies.
rows.anchor: قال عمر، رضي الله عنه: فلو علمت أنكما كتبتما منه شيئا جعلتكما نكالا لهذه الأمة

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Al-Thawri transmits a similar account from Umar through Jabir al-Ju'fi, al-Sha'bi, and Abd Allah ibn Thabit al-Ansari.
rows.anchor: روى الثوري، عن جابر بن يزيد الجعفي، عن الشعبي، عن عبد الله بن ثابت الأنصاري، عن عمر بن الخطاب

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Abu Dawud also transmits a similar report from Umar in his Mursalat, through Abu Qilaba.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو داود في المراسيل، من حديث أبي قلابة، عن عمر نحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to recount Yusuf's story; Yusuf's father was Jacob.
rows.anchor: وأبوه هو: يعقوب، عليه السلام

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: The Prophet calls Yusuf the noble son of a noble lineage: Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Asked about the most honored person, the Prophet first names the God-fearing, then Yusuf as son of a prophet, prophet, and God's intimate friend; he adds that the best in pre-Islamic times are best in Islam when learned in religion.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أي الناس أكرم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Prophets' dreams are revelation.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: رؤيا الأنبياء وحي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Exegetes including Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, Qatada, al-Thawri, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd identify the eleven stars as Yusuf's brothers, sun and moon as his parents; fulfillment came when they bowed before him, after forty or, by another report, eighty years.
rows.anchor: أن الأحد عشر كوكبا عبارة عن إخوته، وكانوا أحد عشر رجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir relays a report attributed to Jaber: a Jewish questioner asked for the stars' names; after Gabriel informed him, the Prophet listed them and the man affirmed them.
rows.anchor: قال: أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رجل من يهود يقال له

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: In Abu Ya'la's added wording, Jacob says the scattered matter will later be assembled by God and identifies the sun as himself and the moon as Yusuf's mother.
rows.anchor: هذا أمر متشتت يجمعه الله من بعد؛ قال: والشمس أبوه، والقمر أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The star-naming report is unique through al-Hakam ibn Zahir al-Fazari, whom leading scholars weakened, most abandoned, and al-Jawzajani called discarded.
rows.anchor: وقد ضعفه الأئمة، وتركه الأكثرون، وقال الجوزجاني: ساقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob understands the dream as the brothers submitting to and greatly honoring Yusuf, so he fears they will envy and plot against him; “plotting” means devising a scheme against him.
rows.anchor: تعبيرها خضوع إخوته له وتعظيمهم إياه تعظيما زائدا

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet instructs a person who sees a pleasing dream to tell it, but after a distressing dream to turn over, spit left three times, seek refuge, and tell no one.
rows.anchor: إذا رأى أحدكم ما يحب فليحدث به، وإذا رأى ما يكره فليتحول إلى جنبه الآخر

rows.speaker: معاوية بن حيدة القشيري
rows.claim: The Prophet says a dream remains on a bird's foot until interpreted; once interpreted, it occurs.
rows.anchor: من رواية معاوية بن حيدة القشيري أنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This teaches concealing a blessing until it appears; a related report says to conceal the pursuit of needs because every blessed person is envied.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا يؤخذ الأمر بكتمان النعمة حتى توجد وتظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God chose Yusuf and showed him the celestial bodies bowing, He chooses and selects him for prophethood.
rows.anchor: ربك} أي: يختارك ويصطفيك لنبوته

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and others understand “interpretation of reports” as interpretation of dreams.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد وغير واحد: يعني تعبير الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing God's blessing for Yusuf means sending him as a messenger and revealing to him.
rows.anchor: ويتم نعمته عليك} أي: بإرسالك والإيحاء إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view calls Isaac the son offered in sacrifice, but Ibn Kathir says that is not the stronger position.
rows.anchor: ولده، وهو الذبيح في قول، وليس بالرجيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is all-knowing and wise, knowing where to place His messengerships.
rows.anchor: أعلم حيث يجعل رسالاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf's story contains lessons and admonitions for those asking about it, because it is an astonishing account worth investigating.
rows.anchor: آيات، أي عبرة ومواعظ للسائلين عن ذلك، المستخبرين عنه، فإنه خبر عجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers swore that Yusuf and his full brother Benjamin were dearer to Jacob than they were, despite their greater numbers; they called Jacob misguided for favoring and loving the two more.
rows.anchor: أي: جماعة، فكيف أحب ذينك الاثنين أكثر من الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No evidence establishes that Yusuf's brothers were prophets; the passage's apparent sense points against it, and the claim that they later received revelation requires proof.
rows.anchor: لم يقم دليل على نبوة إخوة يوسف، وظاهر هذا السياق يدل على خلاف ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usual appeal to 2:136 does not prove the brothers themselves were prophets: “tribes” can mean Israelite clans generally, like Arab tribes or non-Arab peoples.
rows.anchor: لأن بطون بني إسرائيل يقال لهم: الأسباط، كما يقال للعرب: قبائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers propose killing or banishing the rival for Jacob's affection so they can have their father to themselves, intending to repent and become righteous afterward.
rows.anchor: فأضمروا التوبة قبل الذنب

rows.speaker: قتادة ومحمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: They identify the brother who counseled against killing Yusuf as the eldest, Reuben.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة، ومحمد بن إسحاق: كان أكبرهم واسمه روبيل

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies Judah as the brother who counseled against killing Yusuf.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: الذي قال ذلك يهوذا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies Simeon as the brother who counseled against killing Yusuf.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو شمعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not kill Yusuf” means not to take their enmity and hatred to the point of murder; God had a destined plan for his prophethood and rule in Egypt and turned them toward the well plan.
rows.anchor: في عداوته وبغضه إلى قتله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the well was the well of Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: وهي بئر بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal that a passing caravan would find Yusuf would spare the brothers from killing him; “if you are resolved” refers to their determination to act.
rows.anchor: المارة من المسافرين، فتستريحوا بهذا، ولا حاجة إلى قتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers' deed was a grave severing of kinship and disobedience: they lacked pity for a helpless young child and harmed their elderly, frail father by separating him from his beloved son.
rows.anchor: لقد اجتمعوا على أمر عظيم، من قطيعة الرحم، وعقوق الوالد، وقلة الرأفة بالصغير

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq's condemnation stresses Jacob's age, weakness, dignity, standing with God, and need for his son; may God forgive the brothers, for they undertook something immense.
rows.anchor: يغفر الله لهم وهو أرحم الراحمين، فقد احتملوا أمرا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers' assurances of trust and sincere counsel are a pretext, since jealousy makes them intend the opposite.
rows.anchor: وهذه توطئة وسلف ودعوى، وهم يريدون خلاف ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reciters read both verbs with yāʾ: “يرتع ويلعب.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم بالياء {يرتع ويلعب}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the activity as moving about and being energetic; Qatada, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and others agree.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يسعى وينشط. وكذا قال قتادة، والضحاك والسدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their promise to guard Yusuf means they will protect and watch over him for Jacob's sake.
rows.anchor: يقولون: ونحن نحفظه ونحوطه من أجلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says separation pains him because of his intense love for Yusuf and the great good, prophetic character, and moral and physical perfection he sees in him.
rows.anchor: وذلك لفرط محبته له، لما يتوسم فيه من الخير العظيم، وشمائل النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob fears a wolf could eat Yusuf while the brothers are occupied with throwing and tending their flocks and fail to notice.
rows.anchor: أن تشتغلوا عنه برميكم ورعيتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers seize the wolf excuse and say that if it ate Yusuf despite their strength in numbers, they would be helpless losers.
rows.anchor: لئن عدا عليه الذئب فأكله من بيننا، ونحن جماعة، إنا إذا لهالكون عاجزون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All the brothers agreed to cast Yusuf into the well's bottom, while outwardly they had taken him away with affection to please him.
rows.anchor: هذا فيه تعظيم لما فعلوه أنهم اتفقوا كلهم على إلقائه في أسفل ذلك الجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Jacob hugged and kissed Yusuf and prayed for him when sending him with the brothers.
rows.anchor: لما بعثه معهم ضمه إليه، وقبله ودعا له

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and others say the brothers began verbal and physical abuse once out of Jacob's sight, lowered Yusuf by rope, struck him, cut the rope, and he fell into the water before climbing onto a rock called al-Raghoufa.
rows.anchor: السدي وغيره: إنه لم يكن بين إكرامهم له وبين إظهار الأذى له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's revelation in Yusuf's distress comforted and steadied him with a promise of relief, eventual victory over his brothers, and elevation in rank.
rows.anchor: تطييبا لقلبه، وتثبيتا له

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada explain “while they did not realize” as the brothers not realizing that God had revealed to Yusuf.
rows.anchor: قتادة: {وهم لا يشعرون} بإيحاء الله إليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Yusuf would later tell them what they had done when they did not recognize him.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ستنبئهم بصنيعهم هذا في حقك، وهم لا يعرفونك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that Yusuf recognized his brothers in Egypt while they did not recognize him; he tapped the cup and exposed their betrayal, the false wolf story, and the bloodied shirt, saying he believes this verse was revealed about them.
rows.anchor: سمعت ابن عباس يقول: لما دخل إخوة يوسف على يوسف فعرفهم وهم له منكرون

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash says Yusuf remained in the well for three days.
rows.anchor: فمكث في البئر ثلاثة أيام، فيما قاله أبو بكر بن عياش

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the brothers watched by the well all day; a caravan's water-drawer lowered his bucket, Yusuf clung to it, and the man pulled him out and rejoiced at finding a boy.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: لما ألقاه إخوته جلسوا حول البئر يومهم ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reciters read “يا بشرى”; al-Suddi unusually treats Bushra as the name of the water-drawer calling his companion.
rows.anchor: زعم السدي أنه اسم رجل ناداه ذلك الرجل الذي أدلى دلوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man-name explanation is rare and had not previously been given for this reading except in a report from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول من السدي غريب؛ لأنه لم يسبق إلى تفسير هذه القراءة بهذا إلا في رواية عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading instead addresses one's own glad tidings, omitting the possessive yāʾ, as Arabs do in “O self, be patient” and “O boy, come”; the alternate reading clarifies it.
rows.anchor: ويكون قد أضاف البشرى إلى نفسه، وحذف ياء الإضافة وهو يريدها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Suddi, and Ibn Jarir say the water-drawers concealed Yusuf as merchandise, claiming they had bought him from the water people lest others claim a share.
rows.anchor: قاله مجاهد، والسدي، وابن جرير. هذا قول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: By another view from Ibn Abbas, the brothers concealed their kinship and Yusuf concealed his identity for fear they would kill him; they chose to sell him after telling the caravan's water-drawer about him.
rows.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew what Yusuf's brothers and buyers were doing and could have stopped it, but allowed it to proceed under His wisdom and decree.
rows.anchor: يعلم ما يفعله إخوة يوسف ومشتروه، وهو قادر على تغيير ذلك ودفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This indirectly reassures Muhammad that God knows his people's harm, will give them respite, then grant him the outcome and rule as He did Yusuf.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا تعريض لرسوله محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ikrima say Yusuf's brothers sold him for a paltry price.
rows.anchor: يقول تعالى: وباعه إخوته بثمن قليل، قاله مجاهد وعكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basic sense of “بخس” is shortfall or deficiency, as in 72:13; the brothers had little desire for Yusuf and would have given him away freely.
rows.anchor: أي: اعتاض عنه إخوته بثمن دون قليل، وكانوا مع ذلك فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak refer the pronoun in “they sold him” to Yusuf's brothers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والضحاك: إن الضمير

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada instead refers the pronoun in “they sold him” to the caravan travelers.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: بل هو عائد على السيارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers the brothers as the pronoun's antecedent: “they were uninterested” fits the brothers, while the caravan rejoiced at finding Yusuf and kept him as merchandise.
rows.anchor: إنما أراد إخوته، لا أولئك السيارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “بخس” can be glossed as unlawful or unjust, but those are not intended here; the intended sense is deficient or counterfeit, or both, since the price was inherently unlawful anyway.
rows.anchor: وهذا وإن كان كذلك، لكن ليس هو المراد هنا؛ لأن هذا معلوم يعرفه كل أحد

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, Nauf al-Bikali, al-Suddi, Qatada, and Atiyya al-Awfi report a price of twenty dirhams; Atiyya says the brothers divided two dirhams each.
rows.anchor: فعن ابن مسعود باعوه بعشرين درهما، وكذا قال ابن عباس، ونوف البكالي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid gives the price as twenty-two dirhams.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: اثنان وعشرون درهما

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق وعكرمة
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq and Ikrima give the price as forty dirhams.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق وعكرمة: أربعون درهما

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak explains the brothers' lack of desire by saying they did not know Yusuf's prophethood and status with God.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك في قوله: {وكانوا فيه من الزاهدين}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the brothers followed the caravan urging them to secure Yusuf so he could not escape; he was brought to Egypt, offered himself for purchase, and the Muslim king bought him.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: لما باعوه جعلوا يتبعونهم ويقولون لهم: استوثقوا منه لا يأبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God arranged for Yusuf's Egyptian purchaser to care for and honor him, instruct his household to treat him well, and foresee good in him.
rows.anchor: أنه قيض له الذي اشتراه من مصر، حتى اعتنى به وأكرمه، وأوصى أهله به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Awfi reports from Ibn Abbas that the Egyptian Aziz was named Qutayfir.
rows.anchor: العوفي، عن ابن عباس: وكان اسمه قطفير

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq names the Aziz Itfir ibn Ruhayhib, Egypt's treasurer under King al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid, and names his wife Ra'il daughter of Ra'ail.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: اسمه إطفير

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another source gives the Aziz's wife's name as Zulaikha.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: اسمها زليخا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq, through Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib and Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas, identifies the man who sold Yusuf in Egypt as Malik ibn Da'r ibn Buwaiyib ibn Anaqa ibn Midyan ibn Ibrahim.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن السائب، عن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس: كان الذي باعه بمصر مالك بن دعر

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud names three notably perceptive people: Egypt's Aziz, the woman who recommended Moses as a strong, trustworthy hire, and Abu Bakr for appointing Umar.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود أنه قال: أفرس الناس ثلاثة: عزيز مصر حين قال لامرأته

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi say God's empowering Yusuf in Egypt and teaching him interpretation of reports means teaching him dream interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد والسدي: هو تعبير الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's will prevails: when He wills something, no one can resist or oppose it; He overcomes everything else.
rows.anchor: إذا أراد شيئا فلا يرد ولا يمانع ولا يخالف، بل هو الغالب لما سواه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr glosses “God prevails over His affair” as God doing whatever He wills.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {والله غالب على أمره}
